description:
Equipe multidisciplinar de estudantes de STEM com forte base em engenharia e computação. Nosso objetivo é unir observações da Terra da NASA, ciência do solo e tecnologias inteligentes para criar soluções eficientes e sustentáveis. 

Focamos em apoiar o médio e pequeno agricultor a superar os desafios da variabilidade climática, otimizar a gestão de recursos hídricos e navegar pelas incertezas do mercado com segurança.
summary: Ciclus is a revolutionary decision-making tool built to support millions of small and medium farmers. It delivers tailored crop rotation plans and future scenarios, empowering producers to adapt proactively to evolving climate challenges and market uncertainties.
details:
• What it does and how it works: Ciclus is an intelligent decision-support system designed for farmers, built upon a robust 30-year historical series of Earth observation data collected by NASA satellites (such as NASA POWER, GPM, and SMAP), combined with agricultural research, climate variability models, and market intelligence. It works by translating complex satellite telemetry and soil properties (such as data from SoilGrids) into practical, intelligible insights. The system features a temporal timeline simulation ("time travel") where users input their location, farm area, and soil type to receive a customized 1-to-5-year crop rotation plan. It is guided by a friendly AI assistant personified by our mascot, "Raul", which translates technical data into simple, accessible language for everyday producers.
  • What are the benefits of this: The core benefit is providing small and medium-scale farmers with clear, actionable guidance on crop rotation (such as alternating cash crops with soil-regenerating cover crops like Urochloa or legumes) to enhance soil health, retain moisture during dry spells, and prevent erosion. Unlike conventional platforms that only focus on future risks, Ciclus empowers producers with a concrete understanding of how past management decisions impacted their land, optimizing both biological resilience and economic stability.
  • What is the intended impact of the project: The intended impact is to scale support for millions of small and medium producers who historically lack technical expertise and financial resources to navigate unpredictable climate shifts and market volatility. By offering this guidance for free and making physical kits accessible via logistics channels like Mercado Livre, Ciclus aims to secure long-term food security, climate resilience, and financial sustainability for vulnerable agricultural communities in regions like the Brazilian Cerrado.
  • What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project: The platform was built utilizing Claude Code as the core development environment, powered by VS Code as the software engine. The application architecture integrates front-end and back-end development using Java and React, coupled with geospatial APIs and datasets including NASA POWER, SoilGrids (ISRIC), FAO EcoCrop, CONAB, and IBGE (SIDRA).
  • How your project is creative: Ciclus’s creative peak lies in its "time travel" feature. While existing tools (such as ZARC or Broto) only evaluate immediate future sowing risks, and others (like ABC-MAP) focus exclusively on long-term projections, Ciclus uniquely allows producers to look backward into concrete historical data and ask: "What if I had planted crop X instead?". By pairing retrospective counterfactual analysis with forward-looking 1-to-5-year rotation scenarios and an engaging agricultural mascot ("Raul"), the tool turns abstract climate data into an intuitive, storytelling-driven experience.
  • What factors your team considered: The team carefully balanced high scientific rigor with extreme practical usability. We considered the socioeconomic constraints and limited technological resources of our target audience (small/medium farmers), ensuring the interface remains intuitive and leigo-friendly (layman-friendly). Furthermore, we factored in local agronomic realities (such as the vulnerability of Cerrado soils to dry spells and erosion), combining environmental sustainability, economic viability, and regional crop compatibility (using Embrapa guidelines) into a single cohesive solution.
